title: Barney Frank on His Role in the Banking Crisis

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·罗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代的夜总会里当DJ时，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍爱的藏品去上班，把DJ台变成这样一个充满活力的、像50年前精美老物件快闪博物馆的地方。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听来自奥彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: When he retired from Congress, Barney Frank's legacy was a piece of legislation designed to prevent another financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 当巴尼·弗兰克从国会退休时，他的政治遗产是一项旨在防止又一次金融危机的立法。

sentences.en: Now, because of what he's done since, many are asking if Frank helped cause another financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 而现在，由于他之后的所作所为，许多人在质问弗兰克是否协助引发了又一次金融危机。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague David Enrich talks to Frank about the banking crisis and the unexpected role that he played in it.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事大卫·恩里奇采访了弗兰克，谈论了银行危机以及他在其中扮演的意想不到的角色。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, March 22nd.
sentences.zh: 今天是3月22日，星期三。

sentences.en: David, as you have been sorting through the causes and the fallout of this banking crisis that we are still very much in the middle of,
sentences.zh: 大卫，在你一直在梳理这场我们正身处其中的银行危机的起因和余波之际，

sentences.en: why is it that you wanted to talk to former Congressman Barney Frank?
sentences.zh: 为什么你会想要采访前国会议员巴尼·弗兰克？

sentences.en: Well, Barney Frank has been in the middle of so much that has been going on.
sentences.zh: 嗯，巴尼·弗兰克一直处于所发生的大量事件的风口浪尖上。

sentences.en: So back in 2008, after the global financial crisis, he was one of the people most responsible for overhauling the system of financial regulation that was in place.
sentences.zh: 所以在2008年全球金融危机之后，他是对现行金融监管体系进行彻底改革负有最大责任的人之一。

sentences.en: And that was a real landmark achievement that he had.
sentences.zh: 那是他取得的一项真正的里程碑式的成就。

sentences.en: And then in the years to come, he kind of switched gears a little bit.
sentences.zh: 然后在随后的几年里，他的立场稍微转变了一下。

sentences.en: He began to support the plan to roll back some of those requirements.
sentences.zh: 他开始支持取消其中部分监管要求的计划。

sentences.en: And then right around the same time they started doing that, he joined the board of a bank that stood to benefit from those rules being weakened.
sentences.zh: 就在他们开始这样做的大致同时，他加入了一家有望从这些放宽的规则中受益的银行的董事会。

sentences.en: And a few years after that, now we're in the present day, that bank was one of the first to fail.
sentences.zh: 几年后的今天，那家银行成了首批倒闭的银行之一。

sentences.en: A lot of people are concerned that it's one of the bellwethers that is setting off this global banking panic.
sentences.zh: 很多人担心它是引发这场全球银行业恐慌的先兆之一。

sentences.en: And so he's gone from being the guy who created the rules to the guy who supported weakening them to the guy whose bank falls victim to this budding financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 因此，他从制定规则的人，变成了支持放宽规则的人，再到其银行沦为这场初露端倪的金融危机牺牲品的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: A kind of hero to villain, perhaps, journey in a pretty short period of time.
sentences.zh: 在相当短的时间内，经历了一场从英雄到恶棍的转变。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So I was really hoping to get a chance to ask him whether he thinks he made some wrong decisions along the way
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很希望能有机会问问他，是否认为自己在一路走来时做出了一些错误的决定，

sentences.en: and whether he thinks the decisions he made in some ways contributed to the mess that we're now in.
sentences.zh: 以及他是否认为自己做出的决定在某种程度上导致了我们现在陷入的困境。

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: Uh, hi, Congressman.
sentences.zh: 呃，您好，议员先生。

sentences.en: Can you hear us?
sentences.zh: 您能听到我们说话吗？

sentences.en: Hello?
sentences.zh: 喂？

sentences.en: So I arranged to speak to him last Thursday, and we originally planned to do it by video chat.
sentences.zh: 所以我安排在上周四与他交谈，我们原本计划通过视频聊天进行。

sentences.en: It turned out he was in the Caribbean.
sentences.zh: 结果发现他在加勒比海。

sentences.en: His Wi-Fi wasn't great.
sentences.zh: 他的Wi-Fi信号不太好。

sentences.en: We had some issues with, I think, his cell phone and his iPad and his iPhone.
sentences.zh: 我们遇到了一些问题，我想是他的手机、iPad和iPhone出了点状况。

sentences.en: All right, hang on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，等等。

sentences.en: Let me make this louder.
sentences.zh: 让我把声音调大点。

sentences.en: Did you call me on his 627 number?
sentences.zh: 你们是用他627结尾的那个号码打给我的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's us calling.
sentences.zh: 对，是我们打的。

sentences.en: Okay, hang on.
sentences.zh: 好吧，等等。

sentences.en: I'm going to make it louder.
sentences.zh: 我要把它调大声点。

sentences.en: And ultimately, we decided to skip the fancy technology and just call him on his cell phone.
sentences.zh: 最终，我们决定放弃那些花哨的技术，直接用手机拨打他的电话。

sentences.en: This is obviously, I'm sure it's been a tough week for you, yeah?
sentences.zh: 这显然……我相信对你来说这是艰难的一周，对吧？

sentences.en: Oh, the toughest thing has been trying to get this connection is tough.
sentences.zh: 哦，最艰难的事情就是尝试建立这个连接，太难了。

sentences.en: And just remind us, David, who was Frank when he becomes involved in the post-financial crisis
sentences.zh: 大卫，提醒一下我们，当弗兰克介入后金融危机时代的

sentences.en: regulatory work that defines his career?
sentences.zh: 监管工作时，他是一个怎样的人？这定义了他的职业生涯。

sentences.en: Well, first of all, in his telling, he's not someone who has any particular interest or experience in bank regulation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，按他自己的说法，他对银行监管并没有任何特别的兴趣或经验。

sentences.en: Barney Frank was someone who'd been in Congress for, I think, 27 years, all of them representing Massachusetts.
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克在国会待了大约27年，全部代表马萨诸塞州。

sentences.en: And he was one of the most progressive members of the House Democratic Caucus.
sentences.zh: 他是众议院民主党党团中最进步的成员之一。

sentences.en: He was also, or at least I thought he was also, the first openly gay member of Congress, although that's something he corrected me on.
sentences.zh: 他也是——或者至少我以为他是——国会中第一位公开同性恋身份的议员，尽管这一点他纠正了我。

sentences.en: I was not the first openly gay member.
sentences.zh: 我不是第一位公开同性恋身份的议员。

sentences.en: I was the second.
sentences.zh: 我是第二位。

sentences.en: I was the first to volunteer it.
sentences.zh: 我是第一个主动公开的。

sentences.en: My colleague, Gary Studge, had been outed, but he was the first to acknowledge it.
sentences.zh: 我的同事加里·斯塔兹曾被曝光过，但我是第一个承认这一点的。

sentences.en: Three or four members had been outed, but they all claimed that they really weren't gay.
sentences.zh: 有三四名议员曾被曝光，但他们都声称自己其实并不是同性恋。

sentences.en: They had just been too drunk.
sentences.zh: 他们只是喝得太醉了。

sentences.en: My view was, if you're too drunk to remember what you're doing, you're too drunk to do it.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，如果你醉得记不清自己在做什么，那你也醉得没资格去做这件事。

sentences.en: And he was a very outspoken proponent of gay rights at a time when not everyone was doing that.
sentences.zh: 在当时并非所有人都在这样做的时候，他是一个非常直言不讳的同性恋权利倡导者。

sentences.en: The reason he got into kind of the financial space in the first place is that he wanted to do more to promote fair housing and affordable housing for people.
sentences.zh: 他之所以一开始会涉足金融领域，是因为他想做更多的事情来为人们争取公平住房和经济适住房。

sentences.en: And he thought that the House Financial Services Committee, that that would be a good perch from which to push that.
sentences.zh: 他认为众议院金融服务委员会将是推动这一目标的良好阵地。

sentences.en: Then, of course, the banking system starts to unravel in 2007 and 2008.
sentences.zh: 然后，当然，银行系统在2007年和2008年开始瓦解。

sentences.en: Take a look at the stock trading.
sentences.zh: 看看股票交易。

sentences.en: It was fast and furious.
sentences.zh: 它迅速而狂暴。

sentences.en: That is a whopping loss of three and a half billion dollars in market value.
sentences.zh: 那是市值高达35亿美元的惊人损失。

sentences.en: In 2008, when J.P.
sentences.zh: 在2008年，当摩根大通

sentences.en: Morgan has to take over Bear Stearns, that's when it starts.
sentences.zh: 不得不接管贝尔斯登时，一切就这样开始了。

sentences.en: Lehman Brothers is going bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 雷曼兄弟正在破产。

sentences.en: Merrill Lynch sold in haste.
sentences.zh: 美林证券被仓促出售。

sentences.en: They should start to hit the fan with the failures.
sentences.zh: 随着倒闭潮的出现，麻烦开始集中爆发了。

sentences.en: And the committee that he's on becomes instead a very powerful and important place from which he can start tackling the work of trying to stabilize the financial system
sentences.zh: 他所在的委员会转变成了一个非常强大且重要的阵地，他可以从这里开始着手稳定金融系统，

sentences.en: and then fix it so that a crisis like that won't happen again.
sentences.zh: 然后对其进行修复，以免再次发生这样的危机。

sentences.en: We are not the Securities Exchange Commission or the control of the currency.
sentences.zh: 我们不是证券交易委员会或货币监理署。

sentences.en: We are not ourselves regulators.
sentences.zh: 我们本身不是监管机构。

sentences.en: We formulate regulatory policy.
sentences.zh: 我们制定监管政策。

sentences.en: Understanding what happened, why it happened, what didn't happen, those are essential elements of formulating policy going forward.
sentences.zh: 理解发生了什么、为什么发生、什么没有发生，这些是制定未来政策的基本要素。

sentences.en: And, of course, that crisis really stemmed from a downturn in the housing market which revealed that many of the country's biggest banks
sentences.zh: 当然，那场危机实际上源于房地产市场的低迷，这表明该国许多最大的银行

sentences.en: had invested a huge amount of their money in the housing market in the form of mortgages and mortgage-backed securities.
sentences.zh: 以抵押贷款和抵押支持证券的形式在房地产市场投入了巨额资金。

sentences.en: And when the downturn started, these banks lost so much money that the entire financial system was suddenly at risk.
sentences.zh: 当经济低迷开始时，这些银行损失了如此多的资金，以至于整个金融系统突然陷入危险之中。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Well, and keep in mind, though, it wasn't just about the banks making bad decisions.
sentences.zh: 嗯，还要记住，这不仅关乎银行做出糟糕的决定。

sentences.en: One of the real revelations of this crisis was that regulators were completely asleep at the wheel.
sentences.zh: 这场危机的一个真正启示是，监管机构完全在梦游。

sentences.en: And so one of the things that Barney Frank starts to look at in the immediate aftermath of this crisis is how do we empower regulators to act more swiftly, more decisively,
sentences.zh: 因此，巴尼·弗兰克在危机刚刚过去后开始研究的事情之一，就是如何赋能监管机构，使其能够更迅速、更果断地采取行动，

sentences.en: and to not just respond to a crisis once it erupts, but to prevent it from erupting in the first place.
sentences.zh: 不仅在危机爆发后做出反应，而且要防止危机首先爆发。

sentences.en: And so Barney Frank teams up with Senator Chris Dodd, and the two of them set out to enact this absolutely sweeping set of financial reforms
sentences.zh: 于是巴尼·弗兰克与参议员克里斯·多德联手，两人着手颁布这一系列具有深远意义的金融改革，

sentences.en: that's going to do everything from empower regulators to require banks to hold greater financial resources.
sentences.zh: 这将无所不包，从赋予监管机构权力到要求银行持有更多金融资源。

sentences.en: It creates a Consumer Protection Bureau.
sentences.zh: 它创建了一个消费者保护局。

sentences.en: But one of the biggest parts of it is that for the 30 or 40 biggest banks in the country, so that's banks with $50 billion or more of assets,
sentences.zh: 但其中最大的一部分是，对于全国大约30到40家最大的银行，也就是资产达到500亿美元或以上的银行，

sentences.en: there's this much more intense system of federal regulation and other requirements.
sentences.zh: 有一套更加严格的联邦监管体系和其他要求。

sentences.en: Those giant banks face.
sentences.zh: 这些巨型银行所面临的。

sentences.en: And so they have to undergo stress tests.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们必须接受压力测试。

sentences.en: They have to have much thicker capital and liquidity cushions.
sentences.zh: 他们必须拥有更厚实的资本和流动性缓冲。

sentences.en: They need to be in a position where regulators can look at them very quickly and have zero doubts about their ability to survive a really intense economic or financial storm.
sentences.zh: 他们需要处于这样一种境地：监管机构可以非常迅速地审视他们，对他们在极端严峻的经济或金融风暴中生存的能力零怀疑。

sentences.en: And David, what was so special about banks bigger than $50 billion?
sentences.zh: 大卫，资产超过500亿美元的银行有什么特别之处？

sentences.en: Well, basically, these were the types of banks that had caused the 2008 crisis.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上，这些就是曾导致2008年危机的银行类型。

sentences.en: And so this cutoff was meant to ensure that banks like that got especially intense supervision and had especially high levels of financial stability,
sentences.zh: 因此，这一分界线的划定是为了确保此类银行获得格外严格的监管，并拥有格外高的财务稳健水平，

sentences.en: so that when the next crisis came around, banks like this would not be on rickety financial foot.
sentences.zh: 以便当下一场危机来临时，这样的银行不会处于摇摇欲坠的财务基础之上。

sentences.en: Soon after taking office, I proposed a set of reforms to empower consumers and investors
sentences.zh: 上任后不久，我提出了一系列改革方案，以赋予消费者和投资者权力，

sentences.en: to bring the shadowy deals that caused this crisis into the light of day
sentences.zh: 将导致这场危机的暗箱交易大白于天下，

sentences.en: and to put a stop to taxpayer bailouts once and for all.
sentences.zh: 并彻底制止纳税人出资救援。

sentences.en: So do you remember the day that President Obama signed the bill into law?
sentences.zh: 那么你还记得奥巴马总统将该法案签署为法律的那一天吗？

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然记得。

sentences.en: Thanks to a lot of people in this room, those reforms will become the law of the land.
sentences.zh: 多亏了房间里的许多人，这些改革将成为国家的法律。

sentences.en: For the last year, Chairman Barney Frank and Chris Dodd have worked day and night.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一年里，主席巴尼·弗兰克和克里斯·多德日夜兼程地工作。

sentences.en: So the emotional response when the president thanked both me and Chris and how our staffs were so enthused and, yeah, it was a very nice day, a great day.
sentences.zh: 所以，当总统感谢我和克里斯时，那种感动的反应，以及我们的工作人员是多么兴奋，是的，那是非常美好的一天，伟大的一天。

sentences.en: And arguably, this is the crowning achievement of Congressman Frank's career.
sentences.zh: 可以说，这是弗兰克议员职业生涯的巅峰之作。

sentences.en: I mean, the bill literally bears his name.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，该法案直接冠以他的名字。

sentences.en: It's called Dodd Frank.
sentences.zh: 它被称为《多德-弗兰克法案》。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: And about two years later, Congressman Frank, who's 72 at the time, decides he's going to retire from Congress.
sentences.zh: 大约两年后，当时72岁的弗兰克议员决定从国会退休。

sentences.en: When I quit, I wanted the question to be, why are you quitting that?
sentences.zh: 当我辞职时，我希望别人提出的问题是，你为什么要辞去这个？

sentences.en: Why did you stay so long?
sentences.zh: 你为什么待了这么久？

sentences.en: And so what was your plan?
sentences.zh: 那你有什么计划？

sentences.en: What were you going to do in your retirement?
sentences.zh: 你在退休后打算做什么？

sentences.en: Well, one, I got married.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，我结婚了。

sentences.en: And I planned to write, mostly, and speak.
sentences.zh: 我打算写作，主要是写作和演讲。

sentences.en: I had decided I wouldn't lobby, not so much ethically.
sentences.zh: 我曾决定不去游说，倒不是出于伦理原因。

sentences.en: I just didn't feel comfortable going back, frankly, to people who had been my colleagues as a supplicant.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我只是觉得作为一个恳求者，回到那些曾是我的同事的人身边会很不舒服。

sentences.en: Maybe it was an alericant.
sentences.zh: 也许这是一种过敏反应。

sentences.en: But, you know, I just didn't want to do that.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，我就是不想那样做。

sentences.en: And then in 2014, he gets invited to return to Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 然后在2014年，他应邀重返国会山。

sentences.en: And why is he invited back?
sentences.zh: 他为什么会被邀请回去？

sentences.en: Well, he was invited back by his former colleagues in the House Financial Services Committee.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他是应他在众议院金融服务委员会的前同事们的邀请回去的。

sentences.en: Thank you very much, Mr. Chairman.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢您，主席先生。

sentences.en: I'd like to welcome the former chairman and longtime veteran of this committee, Mr. Barney Frank.
sentences.zh: 我想欢迎本委员会的前主席和长期资深元老，巴尼·弗兰克先生。

sentences.en: Barney, I've had your portrait hanging over me for just about a year now.
sentences.zh: 巴尼，你的画像悬挂在我头顶已经有一年左右了。

sentences.en: And during that time, I've concluded that just seeing Barney Frank without hearing him is no Barney Frank at all.
sentences.zh: 在这期间，我得出的结论是，只见巴尼·弗兰克其画不见其人，根本算不上真正的巴尼·弗兰克。

sentences.en: And at this point, Dodd-Frank has come under intense, sustained assault, not just from the banking industry, but also from Republicans on Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 此时，《多德-弗兰克法案》正面临来自银行业以及国会山共和党人的密集、持续的攻击。

sentences.en: The Republicans at this point control the House, and they're doing everything in their power to make a public case against Dodd-Frank.
sentences.zh: 共和党人此时控制了众议院，他们正在竭尽全力公开反对《多德-弗兰克法案》。

sentences.en: I'm pleased we all will be able to hear you today, and I hope to hear you remind my Republican
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我们今天都能听到你的发言，我希望听到你提醒我的共和党

sentences.en: colleagues about just how close to the brink we came in 2008, and about why Congress and
sentences.zh: 同事们，我们在2008年离崩溃边缘有多近，以及为什么国会和

sentences.en: the president responded forcefully with your namesake legislation, the Dodd-Frank Wall Street
sentences.zh: 总统会以你的同名立法《多德-弗兰克华尔街改革和消费者保护法》

sentences.en: Reform and Consumer Protection Act.
sentences.zh: 做出有力回应。

sentences.en: The Democrats on the committee are trying their best to defend the law, but are struggling, especially because they're in the minority.
sentences.zh: 委员会中的民主党人正在尽最大努力捍卫这项法律，但举步维艰，特别是由于他们处于少数派地位。

sentences.en: And so Congressman Frank is invited to come back to Capitol Hill to testify in defense of the law that he helped write.
sentences.zh: 因此，弗兰克议员应邀重返国会山，为他协助起草的法律进行辩护作证。

sentences.en: Chairman, it said that the financial reform bill is as damaging as the health care bill.
sentences.zh: 主席先生，据说金融改革法案与医疗保健法案一样具有破坏性。

sentences.en: Well, my recollection is that this Republican Congress votes on a fairly regular basis to repeal the health care bill.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，这个由共和党掌控的国会相当定期地投票废除医疗保健法案。

sentences.en: Well, where's your bill to repeal the financial reform bill?
sentences.zh: 那么，你们废除金融改革法案的法案在哪里呢？

sentences.en: If you have the courage of your convictions, let's bring it on.
sentences.zh: 如果你对自己的信念有信心，那就把它拿出来吧。

sentences.en: I think the problem is that the public is, in fact, much more supportive of it, and particularly of the Consumer Bureau.
sentences.zh: 我认为问题在于，公众实际上对它的支持度要高得多，尤其是对消费者保护局的支持。

sentences.en: Most of his testimony is spent defending the law.
sentences.zh: 他的大部分证词都花在了捍卫这项法律上。

sentences.en: Nobody is pointed to any abusive practice that I can see.
sentences.zh: 据我所见，没有人指出任何虐待行为。

sentences.en: No one is pointed to any unfair intrusion into the business models.
sentences.zh: 没有人指出任何对商业模式的不公平干预。

sentences.en: And kind of shooting down many of the industry's arguments and the Republican arguments about
sentences.zh: 并且驳斥了许多业界和共和党人的观点，即

sentences.en: the harm that the intense regulation has supposedly done to the banking industry and to the economy.
sentences.zh: 严格的监管据称对银行业和经济造成的损害。

sentences.en: But partway through his testimony, he makes what I regarded as a really surprising concession.
sentences.zh: 但在作证进行到一半时，他做出了我認為非常令人惊讶的让步。

sentences.en: Should a bank's systemic importance be based strictly and solely on their asset size?
sentences.zh: 一家银行的系统重要性是否应该严格且仅仅基于其资产规模？

sentences.en: Well, I do think $50 billion is – well, look, any number is arbitrary, obviously, in the nature of the case.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实认为500亿美元是——好吧，你看，在这种情况的本质下，任何数字显然都是随意的。

sentences.en: He said that the threshold at which the intense federal supervision really kicked in, so that's at $50 billion,
sentences.zh: 他说，严格的联邦监管真正开始发挥作用的门槛，也就是500亿美元，

sentences.en: he acknowledged that he thought now that that threshold was too low, that it was basically snaring too many banks that were not the very biggest of the big
sentences.zh: 他承认，现在他认为这个门槛太低了，它基本上把许多并非规模最大的银行也卷入了

sentences.en: in just an unnecessarily complicated and onerous system of regulation.
sentences.zh: 一个不必要地复杂且繁重的监管体系中。

sentences.en: And he said that this threshold should be a lot higher than it currently was.
sentences.zh: 并且他说这个门槛应该比目前的高得多。

sentences.en: Basically, I think what you ought to do is to set a fairly high number as the automatic cutoff.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我认为你该做的是把自动截断的门槛设得相当高。

sentences.en: You always have to pick a number, and it will always be somewhat arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 你总得选一个数字，而它也总会带有某种主观性。

sentences.en: But yeah, I think that we should look at that $50 billion again.
sentences.zh: 不过，嗯，我觉得我们应该重新审视那500亿美元。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 唔。

sentences.en: So he's opening the door to the possibility of rolling back what seems like a pretty key element of Dodd-Frank, this law that bears his name.
sentences.zh: 因此，他正为撤销《多德-弗兰克法案》中看似相当核心的要素敞开大门，也就是这部以他名字命名的法律。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And it's around this time that Barney Frank is invited to join the board of directors of a regional bank based in New York, and it's called Signature Bank.
sentences.zh: 正是在这个时候，巴尼·弗兰克应邀加入了一家总部位于纽约的区域性银行的董事会，这家银行叫签名银行。

sentences.en: And David, what should we know about Signature Bank at this moment, that they ask Frank to join their board?
sentences.zh: 大卫，关于签名银行，我们在这个时候应该了解些什么，以至于他们会邀请弗兰克加入董事会？

sentences.en: Well, like a lot of other large regional banks in the country, it was growing very quickly, and it was rapidly approaching having $50 billion in assets,
sentences.zh: 嗯，就像国内许多其他大型区域性银行一样，它发展极其迅速，资产规模很快就要接近500亿美元了，

sentences.en: which meant that as the rules were currently written, it was either going to need to really slam on the brakes and stop growing,
sentences.zh: 这意味着按照当时的规则，它要么得狠狠踩下刹车、停止增长，

sentences.en: or it was about to face a whole new intense level of federal oversight and all sorts of new financial requirements that it looked upon very unfavorably.
sentences.zh: 要么就得面临全新且严厉的联邦监管级别，以及各种它极其反感的全新财务要求。

sentences.en: And so at the time that this bank invited Congressman Frank to join its board of directors,
sentences.zh: 因此，在这家银行邀请弗兰克议员加入其董事会时，

sentences.en: Signature had a tremendous amount at stake in the debate over whether or not to raise this $50 billion threshold.
sentences.zh: 在是否提高这500亿美元门槛的辩论中，签名银行有着巨大的利害关系。

sentences.en: So you were approached by Signature Bank.
sentences.zh: 所以签名银行找过你。

sentences.en: What was their pitch?
sentences.zh: 他们的说辞是什么？

sentences.en: They thought I was smart, knew a lot about banking, and had the right values.
sentences.zh: 他们认为我很聪明，对银行业了解很多，并且拥有正确的价值观。

sentences.en: They also stressed to me that they were the leading user of the low-income housing tax credit.
sentences.zh: 他们还向我强调，他们是低收入住房税收抵免政策的主要使用者。

sentences.en: They knew that housing had been my single biggest substantive policy concern.
sentences.zh: 他们知道住房一直是我最关心的单一实质性政策问题。

sentences.en: And in 2015, Frank joins the board of Signature Bank.
sentences.zh: 2015年，弗兰克加入了签名银行的董事会。

sentences.en: This, of course, is both extremely common and extremely criticized, this phenomenon of former members of Congress or former regulators who have spent their careers
sentences.zh: 这当然既极其普遍又备受诟病，前国会议员或前监管机构官员这种现象——他们职业生涯的大部分时间

sentences.en: championing or fighting an issue, later on getting hired by companies who want to use those lawmakers' expertise to navigate that very same issue.
sentences.zh: 都在支持或反对某项议题，随后却被那些希望利用这些议员的专业知识来处理同一议题的公司所雇佣。

sentences.en: It's kind of known as the great revolving door in Washington between government and business.
sentences.zh: 这在华盛顿政界和商界之间，被称为著名的旋转门现象。

sentences.en: So what does Barney Frank say about this decision to join the revolving door system by being on Signature's board?
sentences.zh: 那么，对于通过加入签名银行董事会来涉足旋转门体系这一决定，巴尼·弗兰克是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, he's very candid about why he wanted to be on the board.
sentences.zh: 首先，对于自己为什么想进董事会，他非常坦率。

sentences.en: I wanted to earn money.
sentences.zh: 我想赚钱。

sentences.en: I had no pension.
sentences.zh: 我没有退休金。

sentences.en: I had voluntarily decided not to get into the pension plan in 81.
sentences.zh: 在81年时，我自愿决定不加入退休金计划。

sentences.en: I didn't want to lobby.
sentences.zh: 我不想当游说者。

sentences.en: So I was looking to earn money.
sentences.zh: 所以我当时在寻找赚钱的途径。

sentences.en: I had been making money from speeches, and I had a good advance.
sentences.zh: 我通过演讲赚过钱，而且我有一笔不错的预付款。

sentences.en: I got a half-million-dollar advance to write my memoir.
sentences.zh: 我写回忆录拿到了50万美元的预付款。

sentences.en: But I was planning to live for many more years, and I was looking for an ongoing source of income.
sentences.zh: 但我打算再活很多年，所以我在寻找一个持续的收入来源。

sentences.en: Over the seven-plus years they served on Signature's board, he earned over $2 million.
sentences.zh: 在担任签名银行董事的七年多时间里，他赚了200多万美元。

sentences.en: And this is someone who, as he puts it, has devoted his whole life to public service.
sentences.zh: 而这正是那个用他自己的话说“将一生奉献给公共服务”的人。

sentences.en: He's left an enormous amount of money on the table compared to what he could have made if he was in the private sector.
sentences.zh: 与如果他留在私营部门本可以赚到的钱相比，他放弃了一大笔财富。

sentences.en: And he pointed out to me that, look, he graduated from Harvard Law School.
sentences.zh: 他向我指出，你看，他可是哈佛法学院毕业的。

sentences.en: For about $325,000 a year, which I must say for, you know, it sounds a little arrogant.
sentences.zh: 大约一年32.5万美元，我必须说，这听起来可能有点傲慢。

sentences.en: But for an honors graduate of Harvard Law School, $325,000 a year is not an excessive salary.
sentences.zh: 但对于哈佛法学院的优秀毕业生来说，一年32.5万美元并不是一个过高的薪水。

sentences.en: You look at most graduates of Harvard Law School, they go into big corporate law firms, and they end up making millions and millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 你看看大多数哈佛法学院的毕业生，他们进入大型企业律所，最终赚到的是几百万甚至上千万美元。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fair.
sentences.zh: 也对。

sentences.en: For him, this is just what he's kind of got coming and what he deserves.
sentences.zh: 对他来说，这只是他应得的，也是他理所应得的报酬。

sentences.en: And the second thing, the broad point he makes, is that he doesn't see any particular problem with the revolving door, at least not as it applies to him.
sentences.zh: 第二点，他提出的宏观观点是，他看不出旋转门有什么大问题，至少在适用于他个人的方面是如此。

sentences.en: And so he doesn't think that there is any real issue with someone who had a very important hand in shaping financial regulation and who has recently switched stances and is calling for at least a slight weakening of those regulations.
sentences.zh: 因此，他认为，某个在制定金融监管方面发挥过极其重要作用、而最近又转变立场并呼吁稍微削弱这些监管的人，之间并不存在什么真正的冲突。

sentences.en: He doesn't think there's any conflict of interest or anything wrong with him going, essentially, to work for that company.
sentences.zh: 他认为不存在任何利益冲突，去为那家公司工作也完全没有什么不对。

sentences.en: I don't understand the argument that anything that I advocated as a member of Congress, I shouldn't join in trying to promote afterwards.
sentences.zh: 我不明白这种论点：我在国会任职期间主张过的任何事情，我卸任后就不能参与推广。

sentences.en: And by the way, I was not on the payroll, because I was not an employee.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我不在工资名单上，因为我不是雇员。

sentences.en: I was under no obligation to follow a party line.
sentences.zh: 我没有义务遵循任何政党路线。

sentences.en: In fact, I was literally an independent director.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我名副其实是一名独立董事。

sentences.en: So the argument that I was somehow for hire and that my opinion would be influenced, no.
sentences.zh: 所以那种认为我受之雇佣、我的意见会受到影响的说法，根本没有。

sentences.en: So, David, what happens next?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，接下来发生了什么？

sentences.en: What happens next is that Donald Trump gets elected president.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的是唐纳德·特朗普当选总统。

sentences.en: And on the campaign trail and once in the White House, Trump has made a mission out of destroying Dodd-Frank.
sentences.zh: 在竞选期间以及入主白宫后，特朗普把摧毁《多德-弗兰克法案》当成了一项使命。

sentences.en: He hates it.
sentences.zh: 他恨透了它。

sentences.en: And with Republicans in control of both Congress and the White House, the odds of Dodd-Frank not just being tweaked or relaxed, but being destroyed entirely,
sentences.zh: 随着共和党人同时掌控了国会和白宫，《多德-弗兰克法案》不仅仅是被微调或放松，而是被彻底摧毁的可能性，

sentences.en: go from being kind of a Republican dream into something that is a real possibility.
sentences.zh: 从一个共和党人的梦想变成了现实存在的可能。

sentences.en: And while he's no longer Congressman Frank, now he's just Barney Frank, he endorses a compromise.
sentences.zh: 虽然他不再是弗兰克议员，现在他只是巴尼·弗兰克，但他支持一项妥协方案。

sentences.en: And the heart of it is to increase the $50 billion threshold, after which a bank is subjected to extra intense oversight, for that to go from $50 billion to $250 billion.
sentences.zh: 其核心是将50亿美元的门槛提高——超过这个门槛的银行将接受极其严格的监管——让这个门槛从50亿美元提高到2500亿美元。

sentences.en: So what that means is that the number of banks that are subjected to this extra scrutiny, it goes from a few dozen to just one dozen.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，接受这种额外审查的银行数量，从几十家减少到了仅仅一打。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: It dramatically reduces the number of banks that are coming under this intense microscope.
sentences.zh: 这大幅减少了受到这种严密审视的银行数量。

sentences.en: Even Barney Frank has had some misgivings over this law.
sentences.zh: 甚至连巴尼·弗兰克对这部法律也有所保留。

sentences.en: The fact that Barney Frank was such a well-respected member, especially on the left, and had played such a pivotal role in writing this law to the first place,
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克曾是一位备受尊敬的议员，尤其在左翼阵营中，并且在当初起草这部法律时发挥了举足轻重的作用，

sentences.en: meant that his endorsement of increasing this threshold carried an enormous amount of weight all over Capitol Hill.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他对比提高这一门槛的背书，在整个国会山具有巨大的分量。

sentences.en: Even former chairman of the Financial Services Committee, Chairman Barney Frank, when he wrote about the threshold, he wrote that, quote, it is, quote, arbitrary.
sentences.zh: 甚至连金融服务委员会前主席巴尼·弗兰克议员，在谈到这个门槛时也写道，“它是”引述，“随意的”。

sentences.en: We're going to say this all day, Barney Frank even thinks the threshold is too low, it can be fixed.
sentences.zh: 我们要整天这么说，连巴尼·弗兰克都觉得门槛太低了，这可以修补。

sentences.en: Republicans started citing this.
sentences.zh: 共和党人开始引用这一点。

sentences.en: And on the $50 billion threshold, he said, I think it should be changed.
sentences.zh: 而关于50亿美元的门槛，他说，我认为应该改变。

sentences.en: Democrats started citing it.
sentences.zh: 民主党人也开始引用这一点。

sentences.en: Congressman Barney Frank said about 95% of Dodd-Frank, as it is written, will remain intact after this bill passes.
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克议员表示，该法案通过后，《多德-弗兰克法案》现有内容的大约95%将保持不变。

sentences.en: Again, this is former chairman Frank, of his own signature law, said the $50 billion threshold was arbitrary and a mistake.
sentences.zh: 再次强调，这是弗兰克前主席针对他自己亲手签名的法律，称50亿美元的门槛是随意的，是个错误。

sentences.en: And he's right.
sentences.zh: 他是对的。

sentences.en: And in 2018.
The legislation I'm signing today rolls back the crippling Dodd-Frank regulations.
sentences.zh: 我今天签署的立法废除了束缚手脚的《多德-弗兰克法案》监管规定。

sentences.en: President Trump signs it into law.
sentences.zh: 特朗普总统将其签署成法律。

sentences.en: And you see, almost immediately, the banks start to take advantage of this.
sentences.zh: 你看，几乎立刻，各大银行就开始利用这一点。

sentences.en: Silicon Valley Bank, for example, goes from being right under this $50 billion threshold, it more than quadruples in size in the space of just a couple years.
sentences.zh: 例如，硅谷银行从刚好低于这个50亿美元门槛的规模，在短短几年内扩大了四倍多。

sentences.en: Signature, where Barney Frank is on the board, goes from right under the threshold, it more than doubles in the space of a few years.
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克担任董事的签名银行，从刚好低于门槛的规模，在几年内扩大了两倍多。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: So, with Barney Frank's help, two of the banks that will eventually help trigger this banking crisis that we're still living through are allowed to become much,
sentences.zh: 因此，在巴尼·弗兰克的帮助下，最终引发我们仍在经历的这场银行业危机的两家银行，得以在监管大幅放松的情况下变得大得

sentences.zh: 多得多。

sentences.zh: 由于担心其财务状况摇摇欲坠，硅谷银行遭遇挤兑。

sentences.zh: 在他的讲述中，问题直到监管机构接管硅谷银行的那个周五下午才真正开始。

sentences.zh: 签名银行实质上面临着自身的银行挤兑。

sentences.en: The bank officers are then working on trying to persuade people not to leave.
sentences.zh: 银行高管随后努力说服人们不要离开。

sentences.en: That becomes clear at first that that's hard to do.
sentences.zh: 起初很明显，这很难做到。

sentences.en: Customers started yanking their deposits as fast as they could.
sentences.zh: 客户开始以最快的速度撤走存款。

sentences.en: And the leadership was concerned that they needed to, A, try to stem the deposits, and, B, try to increase the liquidity to make sure we could fund those deposits.
sentences.zh: 管理层担心他们需要：A，努力遏制存款流失；B，努力增加流动性，以确保我们能够应付这些存款兑付。

sentences.en: So, how bad was it on Friday?
sentences.zh: 那么周五的情况有多糟？

sentences.en: And do you have a sense of how many—
sentences.zh: 你大概知道有多少——

sentences.en: Well, David, what's the point of that?
sentences.zh: 好了，大卫，这有什么意义？

sentences.en: What do you mean, how bad was it?
sentences.zh: 你什么意思，情况有多糟？

sentences.en: Well— Was it one to ten?
sentences.zh: 嗯——是从一到十吗？

sentences.en: And as I'm pushing him on the details of what happened, he got pretty testy at times.
sentences.zh: 当我向他追问事情发生的细节时，他有时会变得相当急躁。

sentences.en: And it felt to me like he was really trying to distance himself from this whole mess.
sentences.zh: 我感觉他真的是在试图与这场乱局划清界限。

sentences.en: I was not at the bank.
sentences.zh: 我当时不在银行。

sentences.en: Right, but what did they lose in terms of deposits?
sentences.zh: 对，但他们在存款方面损失了多少？

sentences.en: Do you want to know what it was like?
sentences.zh: 你想知道当时是什么情况吗？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: How much deposits did they lose?
sentences.zh: 他们损失了多少存款？

sentences.en: I remember the number I got for it was $12 to $14 billion.
sentences.zh: 我记得我得到的数字是120亿到140亿美元。

sentences.en: Something like $12 to $14 billion of deposits fled the bank that afternoon, he says.
sentences.zh: 他说，那天下午有大约120亿到140亿美元的存款逃离了银行。

sentences.en: And that put the bank in a very precarious financial position heading into the weekend.
sentences.zh: 这使得银行在进入周末时处于极其岌岌可危的财务境地。

sentences.en: They began on Saturday, or late Friday and Saturday, working on ways to get more liquidity.
sentences.zh: 他们从周六（或者周五晚些时候和周六）开始寻找获取更多流动性的方法。

sentences.en: But there was no sense of impending doom.
sentences.zh: 但并没有末日临近的感觉。

sentences.en: There was some confidence Sunday morning that we were stabilizing the deposits.
sentences.zh: 周日早上，大家对我们正在稳定存款还有一些信心。

sentences.en: And it came as a big shock to everybody when the FGIC said we're coming over Sunday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 当联邦存款保险公司（FDIC）说他们周日下午要过来时，对所有人来说都是个巨大的打击。

sentences.en: That was not good news.
sentences.zh: 那可不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: That afternoon, he gets a phone call from the bank's CEO saying that regulators have decided to seize the bank and shut it down.
sentences.zh: 那天下午，他接到银行首席执行官的电话，称监管机构已决定接管并关闭这家银行。

sentences.en: I mean, that must have been an extremely upsetting moment for both of you.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对你们俩来说，那一定是个极其令人心烦意乱的时刻。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Can you tell me a little bit more about how you were feeling, how you reacted?
sentences.zh: 能多跟我讲讲你当时的感受吗，你是怎么反应的？

sentences.en: How did I react?
sentences.zh: 我有什么反应？

sentences.en: I said, oh, that sucks.
sentences.zh: 我说，哦，这真够糟的。

sentences.en: Somehow, knowing you, Congressman, I imagine you were a little more colorful.
sentences.zh: 议员，以我对你的了解，我想你的措辞可能会更生动一些。

sentences.en: David, I hope your chances at a publisher don't depend on your showing how we were upset when we were told our bank was closed.
sentences.zh: 大卫，我希望你能不能找到出版商，不要指望靠展示我们听到银行倒闭时的沮丧心情来决定。

sentences.en: Yeah, I hope so, too.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我也希望如此。

sentences.en: That's not a scoop.
sentences.zh: 这算不上什么独家新闻。

sentences.en: Yeah, I was disappointed.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我是很失望。

sentences.en: He claims that this is a terrible mistake, that this is overzealous regulators coming in to try to make an example out of Signature publicly for having dabbled in cryptocurrencies.
sentences.zh: 他声称这是一个可怕的错误，这是过度热心的监管机构介入，试图以签名银行涉足加密货币为由将其公然树立为反面典型。

sentences.en: And that on the merits, the bank was on stable footing and should not have been shut down.
sentences.zh: 而且从本质上看，该银行基础稳固，本不该被关闭。

sentences.en: And remind us, what was the government's case for taking over Signature Bank?
sentences.zh: 提醒我们一下，政府接管签名银行的理由是什么？

sentences.en: Well, the government has not very clearly articulated the exact rationale.
sentences.zh: 嗯，政府并没有非常清晰地阐明确切的理由。

sentences.en: But what they have said with both Signature and Silicon Valley Bank is that part of what the government was trying to do was protect the stability of the broader financial system.
sentences.zh: 但他们对签名银行和硅谷银行所说的是，政府试图做的一部分事情是保护更广泛金融体系的稳定性。

sentences.en: And what I and I think most people have taken that to mean is that both of these banks had grown so big so quickly that their uncontrolled collapses really posed a pretty serious threat to the stability of the entire American banking system.
sentences.zh: 我和我认为的大多数人对此的理解是，这两家银行扩张太快、规模太大，它们的失控倒闭确实对整个美国银行体系的稳定构成了相当严重的威胁。

sentences.en: Right, and I think that brings us to the heart of why it is you wanted to talk to Frank in the first place.
sentences.zh: 没错，我想这也正是你一开始就想采访弗兰克的核心原因所在。

sentences.en: So what does he say about the unique role he played in rolling back the original Dodd-Frank financial limits,
sentences.zh: 那么，对于他在撤销最初的《多德-弗兰克法案》金融限制中发挥的独特作用，他是怎么说的？

sentences.en: which encouraged Signature to grow so fast with less regulatory oversight than it would have had under the law's original rules?
sentences.zh: 从而促使签名银行在监管较少的情况下迅速发展，而如果按照该法案最初的规则，本不会如此？

sentences.en: Does he think that any of the rules that were in place from the beginning might have stopped a bank like Signature or Silicon Valley from ending up where it did,
sentences.zh: 他是否认为最初制定的任何规则本可以阻止像签名银行或硅谷银行这样的银行走到今天这一步，

sentences.en: under government control, failing as a bank?
sentences.zh: 陷入政府接管、银行倒闭的境地？

sentences.en: The short answer is no.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，不会。

sentences.en: He does not think it would have made a whole lot of difference at all.
sentences.zh: 他认为这根本不会产生太大的区别。

sentences.en: There's nothing – the stress test would not have predicted the problem of Silicon Valley.
sentences.zh: 根本没有——压力测试本无法预测硅谷银行的问题。

sentences.en: I don't know how we do know in that one's going to be the case.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我们怎么能确信那种情况一定会发生。

sentences.en: And to review, the rules that these biggest banks are subjected to, they have to conduct these annual stress tests to make sure that they can withstand a severe financial storm.
sentences.zh: 回顾一下，这些最大型银行必须遵守的规则是，他们必须每年进行这些压力测试，以确保他们能够经受住严重的金融风暴。

sentences.en: They have to hold more liquidity so they're better positioned in the event of a bank run.
sentences.zh: 他们必须持有更多流动性，以便在发生挤兑时处于更有利的位置。

sentences.en: Paperwork.
sentences.zh: 文书工作。

sentences.en: You have a significant paperwork increase.
sentences.zh: 你的文书工作量大幅增加。

sentences.en: Well, and a significant – the paperwork is not paperwork for paperwork's sake, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且大量的——文书工作并不是为了做文书而做文书，对吧？

sentences.en: It's paperwork because –
sentences.zh: 之所以有文书工作是因为——

sentences.en: No, $50 billion did not trigger any higher liquidity requirement of other rules.
sentences.zh: 不对，500亿美元并没有触发任何其他规则中更高的流动性要求。

sentences.en: And what Barney Frank said to me, which I found kind of surprising and not very precise, is that the additional requirements that were rolled back,
sentences.zh: 巴尼·弗兰克对我说的话，我发现有点意外，而且不是很精确，那就是被废除的附加要求，

sentences.en: they basically amounted to a lot of extra paperwork.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上只是一堆额外的文书工作。

sentences.en: He said they didn't really affect the underlying financial health of these banks and that they wouldn't have prevented this current crisis.
sentences.zh: 他说这些并没有真正影响这些银行潜在的财务健康，而且它们本无法防止当前的危机。

sentences.en: I mean, can I just ask you, David, do you think he's right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我能问一下吗，大卫，你觉得他说得对吗？

sentences.en: Based on my reporting, I don't think that he is.
sentences.zh: 根据我的报道，我认为并不对。

sentences.en: And the stress tests, for example,
sentences.zh: 比如压力测试，

sentences.en: that big banks were supposed to be subjected to are meant to detect situations kind of like the one we're in now to basically make sure that the biggest banks are able to withstand really intense financial crises.
sentences.zh: 本该对大型银行实施的测试，旨在发现类似于我们现在所处的情境，基本上是为了确保最大型银行能够经受住非常剧烈的金融危机。

sentences.en: The extra liquidity requirements that the biggest banks face are supposed to help a bank avoid a bank run, which is exactly what just killed Signature and Silicon Valley Bank.
sentences.zh: 大型银行面临的额外流动性要求本应帮助银行避免挤兑，而这正是刚刚摧毁签名银行和硅谷银行的元凶。

sentences.en: So I think actually that Barney Frank is being a little bit dismissive about the importance of these rules that he had helped write and the potential that they could have really made a big difference.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，巴尼·弗兰克实际上有点轻视这些他曾协助起草的规则的重要性，以及它们本可能产生的巨大影响。

sentences.en: But here's the thing, even if we grant that these extra regulations wouldn't have made a lick of difference in this current situation, nobody disputes the fact that in 2018,
sentences.zh: 但问题是，即使我们承认这些额外的监管在当前情况下不会产生丝毫影响，也没有人否认这样一个事实：在2018年，

sentences.en: when the cap got lifted from $50 billion to $250 billion, that set off an arms race among big regional banks like Signature and Silicon Valley,
sentences.zh: 当门槛从500亿美元提高到2500亿美元时，这在签名银行和硅谷银行这样的大型区域性银行中引发了一场军备竞赛，

sentences.en: where they doubled or quadrupled in size in the space of a few short years.
sentences.zh: 它们在短短几年内规模翻倍甚至翻了两番。

sentences.en: And that is how you've got these banks that are potentially posing a risk to the stability of the overall financial system.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么这些银行现在可能对整个金融系统的稳定性构成风险。

sentences.en: And what does Frank say about that, this seemingly indisputable reality that the change he endorsed to his own law allowed for, even encouraged, this rapid growth?
sentences.zh: 对于这一点，弗兰克是怎么说的？对于他自己法案所支持的修改居然允许甚至鼓励了这种快速增长这一看似无可争辩的现实，他怎么说？

sentences.en: He acknowledges it.
sentences.zh: 他承认了这一点。

sentences.en: The $50 billion acted as a deterrent to some banks for organic growth.
sentences.zh: 500亿美元的门槛确实对一些银行的内生增长起到了威慑作用。

sentences.en: No question.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问。

sentences.en: And I don't think that was a good idea.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那是个好主意。

sentences.en: I don't think it's bad for a bank to be at 80 rather than 50.
sentences.zh: 我不认为银行规模是800亿而不是500亿有什么不好。

sentences.en: I think banks are basically good things.
sentences.zh: 我认为银行基本上是好东西。

sentences.en: They do good things for the economy.
sentences.zh: 它们对经济有益。

sentences.en: They're essential.
sentences.zh: 它们是必不可少的。

sentences.en: And if a bank is prospering by playing a good role, I think it's a good thing that they get bigger.
sentences.zh: 如果一家银行通过扮演好角色而繁荣发展，我认为它变大是一件好事。

sentences.en: The thing that surprised me, coming from Barney Frank, who had spent years kind of blasting the big banks, was that he thought it was actually totally fine and, in fact, positive.
sentences.zh: 让我惊讶的是，出自巴尼·弗兰克之口——他曾花多年时间抨击大型银行——他认为这其实完全没问题，甚至还是积极的。

sentences.en: And I'm saying that I don't see a harm in a bank having $80 billion.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不觉得银行拥有800亿美元有什么坏处。

sentences.en: You seem to have an anti-bank bias.
sentences.zh: 你似乎对银行有偏见。

sentences.en: Well, big banks, they're bad things.
sentences.zh: 好吧，大型银行，它们不是好东西。

sentences.en: I don't think it's...
sentences.zh: 我不认为这是……

sentences.en: That's what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 这就是你的观点。

sentences.en: I think, I guess...
sentences.zh: 我想，我猜……

sentences.en: Yeah, that's what you're saying.
sentences.zh: 是的，这就是你的观点。

sentences.en: Congressman,
sentences.zh: 国会议员，

sentences.en: my starting point on this is that these two big banks failed and that that's caused a lot of stress in the financial system and is scaring a lot of people about what might happen.
sentences.zh: 我对此的出发点是，这两家大银行倒闭了，这给金融系统造成了巨大的压力，并让许多人对可能发生的事情感到恐慌。

sentences.en: But no, I take it back.
sentences.zh: 但等等，我收回刚才的话。

sentences.en: That's not the point I was just funding to get.
sentences.zh: 那不是我刚才真正想表达的重点。

sentences.en: He did not engage, really, when I pushed him on the fact that had these banks not grown as large as they did, as quickly as they did,
sentences.zh: 当我向他追问——如果这些银行没有长得那么大、那么快，

sentences.en: they wouldn't pose the same risk to financial stability that regulators cited when they had to shut down these two banks.
sentences.zh: 它们就不会对监管机构在被迫关闭这两家银行时所提到的金融稳定构成同等风险时，他实际上并没有正面回应。

sentences.en: Yeah, as I said, though, the point I'm trying to get across, maybe not very effectively,
sentences.zh: 是的，不过就像我说的，我试图表达的观点——也许表达得不太有效——

sentences.en: is that the reason that SVB and signatures collapses have been problematic and scary for the financial system, I think, is because they were big.
sentences.zh: 是硅谷银行和签名银行的倒闭之所以会带来麻烦并让金融系统感到恐慌，我认为是因为它们体量庞大。

sentences.en: Because they had grown so quickly.
sentences.zh: 因为它们扩张得太快了。

sentences.en: And...
sentences.zh: 而且……

sentences.en: Oh, no question.
sentences.zh: 哦，毫无疑问。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean no banks were dead bigger than it was bad.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着银行体量变大就是坏事。

sentences.en: And by the way, my prediction is that in two weeks this will have been shown to be not a systemic issue, that it will have been resolved by what the federal regulators did.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我的预测是，两周后事实将证明这不是一个系统性问题，联邦监管机构采取的行动已经解决了这个问题。

sentences.en: Well, no, you think I'm too optimistic.
sentences.zh: 好吧，不，你觉得我太乐观了。

sentences.en: Call me back in two weeks.
sentences.zh: 两周后再给我打电话。

sentences.en: Seriously, let's write about this two weeks from now.
sentences.zh: 说真的，两周后我们再来谈论这个。

sentences.en: Basically, where we ended up is a disagreement about the severity of the current crisis we're in.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我们的分歧在于对当前所处危机严重程度的看法不同。

sentences.en: And his prediction was that this is something, it's kind of a blip.
sentences.zh: 他的预测是，这只是一件小插曲。

sentences.en: This is not a real financial crisis.
sentences.zh: 这不是真正的金融危机。

sentences.en: And two weeks later, no one will even be talking or thinking about this.
sentences.zh: 两周后，甚至没有人会谈论或想起这件事。

sentences.en: Yeah, there were two, three bank failures.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实发生了两三家银行倒闭。

sentences.en: But they didn't trigger anything like the threat of 2008 and 2009, nor did they require remedies anywhere near as extensive.
sentences.zh: 但它们没有引发任何类似于2008年和2009年那样的威胁，也没有需要如此大规模的补救措施。

sentences.en: Yeah, although I think a skeptic or a pessimist might say that this financial crisis, if we can call it that, is not over yet.
sentences.zh: 是的，尽管我认为持怀疑或悲观态度的人可能会说，这场金融危机——如果我们能这样称呼它的话——还没有结束。

sentences.en: Does it occur to you, Davis, that same skeptic might say that Elvis is alive and is behind all this?
sentences.zh: 大卫，你有没有想过，那个持怀疑态度的人可能会说猫王还活着而且是这一切的幕后黑手？

sentences.en: Anybody could say anything.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以说任何话。

sentences.en: Of course, this conversation takes place on a Thursday.
sentences.zh: 当然，这段对话发生在一个星期四。

sentences.en: While we're on the phone, another big bank, First Republic, got bailed out by other banks.
sentences.zh: 就在我们通话时，另一家大银行第一共和银行得到了其他银行的救助。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then 48 hours later, over the weekend, Credit Suisse, which is one of the biggest banks in the world,
sentences.zh: 然后在48小时后的周末，作为全球最大银行之一的瑞士信贷，

sentences.en: essentially has to be rescued by the Swiss government in this huge deal in which they get taken over by another giant bank.
sentences.zh: 基本上不得不通过一项巨额交易接受瑞士政府的救援，被另一家巨型银行收购。

sentences.en: So there's a quality of Frank burying his head a little bit in the sand around just how big a deal this has all become
sentences.zh: 所以，弗兰克在这里有点掩耳盗铃，忽视了这一切变得多么严重，

sentences.en: and the role that the growth of banks that he helped happen played in this crisis.
sentences.zh: 以及他曾推波助澜的银行扩张在这场危机中扮演了什么角色。

sentences.en: Yeah, I don't know if he's burying his head in the sand, and he might turn out to be right.
sentences.zh: 是的，我不知道他是不是在掩耳盗铃，他最终也可能是对的。

sentences.en: And it might be the case that by mid-April, no one is thinking about this as a huge crisis, and this might turn out to be a blip.
sentences.zh: 也许到四月中旬，没有人会把这当作一场巨大的危机，这可能只是一次小插曲。

sentences.en: It's hard to predict the future, but it felt to me like he was contorting himself a little bit
sentences.zh: 预测未来很难，但我感觉他有点在强词夺理，

sentences.en: to make an argument that the changes that he had endorsed really did not have any effect at all.
sentences.zh: 极力辩称他所支持的那些修改其实根本没有任何影响。

sentences.en: And so I asked him at one point in the interview, You were the author of this very important legislation.
sentences.zh: 所以我曾在采访中问他：你是这部非常重要立法的作者。

sentences.en: You then support rolling back portions of that legislation.
sentences.zh: 然后你支持废除该立法的一部分。

sentences.en: And then you end up sitting on the board and getting paid by a company that is a beneficiary of those legislative changes.
sentences.zh: 最后你进入了一家受益于这些立法修改的公司董事会并拿取报酬。

sentences.en: And then, you know, that bank fails.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，那家银行倒闭了。

sentences.en: And that has caused a lot of concern about the stability of the financial system.
sentences.zh: 这引发了人们对金融系统稳定性的极大担忧。

sentences.en: So what's your question?
sentences.zh: 所以你的问题是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I knew all that.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些我都知道。

sentences.en: My answer is that nothing I did was in any way positive of the failure.
sentences.zh: 我的回答是，我所做的一切在任何方面都不是导致倒闭的原因。

sentences.en: And Frank really, at the end of the day, kept pointing to the political reality that he and other Democrats were facing back in 2018 when Dodd-Frank was under attack in Congress.
sentences.zh: 说到底，弗兰克一直指向他和其他民主党人在2018年多德-弗兰克法案在国会遭受攻击时所面临的政治现实。

sentences.en: In fact,
sentences.zh: 事实上，

sentences.en: the reason I advocated changes in part was I thought they were changes that did not in any way diminish the importance of the bill and its impact and were helpful to support politicians who were under pressure to vote for more serious rollbacks.
sentences.zh: 我主张修改的部分原因在于，我认为这些修改在任何程度上都没有削弱该法案的重要性和影响力，并且有助于支持那些面临压力、不得不投票支持更严厉废除法案的政客。

sentences.en: And that's why I supported the notion of removing the politically most inflammatory parts of it that did not interfere with its impact.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我支持剔除其中政治上最具煽动性但又不会干扰其影响力的部分。

sentences.en: So that's that's my answer.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是我的回答。

sentences.en: And I think I feel vindicated by that.
sentences.zh: 我认为这证明我是对的。

sentences.en: He says that at the time, the decision to kind of make this concession on the 50 billion dollar threshold was actually a very savvy political move.
sentences.zh: 他说，当时在500亿美元门槛问题上做出这种妥协其实是一个非常精明的政治举动。

sentences.en: It was basically made to save Dodd-Frank in its entirety.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是为了完整地挽救多德-弗兰克法案。

sentences.en: And his argument was that by making this concession,
sentences.zh: 他的论点是，通过做出这种妥协，

sentences.en: Democrats and Republicans would both support it and would kind of take the momentum away from some of the Republicans who were most intent upon completely gutting or destroying Dodd-Frank.
sentences.zh: 民主党和共和党都会支持它，从而削弱那些执意要彻底阉割或摧毁多德-弗兰克法案的共和党人的势头。

sentences.en: And so in his view, this compromise, even if it's imperfect, it's still preserved Dodd-Frank for the most part in its entirety.
sentences.zh: 所以在他的看法中，这种妥协即使不够完美，仍然在很大程度上完整地保留了多德-弗兰克法案。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the story he's telling you, the story perhaps he's telling himself, is that in order to save Dodd-Frank, he had to weaken it.
sentences.zh: 所以他讲述的故事，也许他自己深信的故事是：为了挽救多德-弗兰克法案，他不得不削弱它。

sentences.en: And saving Dodd-Frank was worth it because that will theoretically prevent a much larger financial crisis than whatever it is we're now in the middle of.
sentences.zh: 挽救多德-弗兰克法案是值得的，因为从理论上讲，这将防止比我们现在所处危机大得多的金融危机。

sentences.en: That's how he's thinking about what has happened here.
sentences.zh: 这就是他对这里发生的事情的看法。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Look, there is no question that had Dodd-Frank been rolled back entirely, I think the financial mess that we're now in would probably be a lot worse.
sentences.zh: 听着，毫无疑问，如果多德-弗兰克法案被彻底废除，我们现在陷入的金融混乱可能会糟糕得多。

sentences.en: But I also think at the same time that this is a bit of an ex post facto justification by him.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时我也认为，这是他的一种事后诸葛亮的辩解。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: For doing something that clearly has put him in a really bright and uncomfortable spotlight.
sentences.zh: 为了给一件明显把他推向刺眼且不舒服聚光灯下的事情开脱。

sentences.en: But he says he just does not really care what other people have to say about him.
sentences.zh: 但他表示，他真的不在乎别人对他的评价。

sentences.en: One of the great pleasures of leaving elected office is that you are no longer subject to an impact from the opinions of people whom you do not respect and do not know.
sentences.zh: 离开民选公职的一大乐趣在于，你不再受那些你不尊重、也不认识的人的意见的影响。

sentences.en: You know, at this point in my life, I don't care.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，在我人生的这个阶段，我不在乎。

sentences.en: So, David, I'm curious, what happens to Barney Frank's job on the board of Signature now that Signature kind of is no more?
sentences.zh: 那么，大卫，我很好奇，既然签名银行已经不复存在了，巴尼·弗兰克在签名银行董事会的工作怎么处理？

sentences.en: It was vaporized the moment regulators seized it.
sentences.zh: 就在监管机构接管它的那一刻，它就灰飞烟灭了。

sentences.en: The board was dissolved and Barney Frank was out of his job.
sentences.zh: 董事会解散了，巴尼·弗兰克失业了。

sentences.en: He seemed okay with that, though.
sentences.zh: 不过他对此似乎挺淡定的。

sentences.en: He told me that he was scheduled to have a board meeting for Signature in New York the day before our interview.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，在我们采访的前一天，他原本计划在纽约参加一个签名银行的董事会会议。

sentences.en: That meeting was canceled, B Signature was done.
sentences.zh: 那个会议取消了，签名银行完蛋了。

sentences.en: And instead, he was able to get an earlier flight down to the Caribbean and just get back to being a private citizen.
sentences.zh: 相反，他得以搭乘较早的航班去加勒比海，重新做回一个普通公民。

sentences.en: Well, David, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，大卫，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 我们知道罢工将是一种牺牲。

sentences.en: But we also know that our families have been sacrificing for far too long on poverty wages in the richest state, in the richest country of the world.
sentences.zh: 但我们也知道，在世界上最富有的州、最富有的国家里，我们的家庭为了维持贫困线以下的工资已经牺牲了太久。

sentences.en: America's second largest public school system ground to a halt on Tuesday as 30,000 school workers in Los Angeles began a three-day strike over what they say is low pay in a city where the cost of living has surged.
sentences.zh: 周二，美国第二大公立学校系统陷入停摆，洛杉矶3万名学校员工开始了一场为期三天的罢工，抗议他们所说的生活成本飙升的城市中的低薪问题。

sentences.en: What do we want?

sentences.en: What do we want?

sentences.en: Now!

sentences.en: The union representing the workers is demanding a 30 percent overall raise.
sentences.zh: 代表这些工人的工会要求整体加薪30%。

sentences.en: City officials have countered with a 23 percent raise and say that the strike will hurt students and their families.
sentences.zh: 市政府官员则反过来提出加薪23%，并表示罢工将伤害学生及其家庭。
